name: Lane

scaling.scaled: Reduce the barbell to a weight that never demands more than two breaks per set, and substitute the gymnastics progressions you'd use in Fran or Diane.
scaling.beginner: Halve the scheme with an empty bar and ring rows — descending-ascending ladders teach set management better than straight sets.

origin.summary: One of the newer Girls: alternating barbell and gymnastics work in a descending-then-ascending scheme that keeps neither the arms nor the lungs fully in charge. Part of CrossFit's original 'Girls' benchmark series — named workouts introduced by founder Greg Glassman starting in 2003, on the logic that anything that leaves you flat on your back deserves a name like a storm. They serve as repeatable fitness tests: revisit one every few months and the clock tells you whether you're fitter. First posted to CrossFit.com on 2021-01-26.

description: Five rounds of max-rep hang power snatches at a bodyweight-relative load and max-rep handstand push-ups, scored by total reps — pairs a loaded pull with strict overhead gymnastics.
source_notes: crossfit.com/faq/wod (official CrossFit FAQ, 'Explain The Workouts with Names (the Girls)?'), retrieved 2026-07-08
